obligation: Part 37 client notice of suspected unauthorized access
citation: Part 37 client contracts (information protection clause); flows down the client's 10 CFR 37.43(d) duty and supports its 37.57(b) assessment
trigger: Actual or suspected access to a client's security plan, implementing procedures, approved-individual list, or review reports by anyone the client has not approved, including an attacker, a public link, or an unapproved AI tool
notify: The client's RSO and security contact by phone, confirmed in writing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the main clock for this runbook

obligation: Part 37 suspicious activity assessment and report (the client's duty)
citation: 10 CFR 37.57(b), applied to Florida clients through their license condition (reports go to the Florida Bureau of Radiation Control)
trigger: The client decides whether the practice's incident is "suspicious activity related to possible theft, sabotage, or diversion" of its category 2 material
deadline: Client assesses; notifies the local law enforcement agency as appropriate; notifies the regulator as soon as possible but no later than 4 hours after notifying the law enforcement agency
notify: Client's duty: local law enforcement agency; Florida Bureau of Radiation Control
applies_at_this_tier: No - the client's duty. The practice gives facts quickly and supports the client's assessment; it does not report for the client

obligation: Reactor client notice of a cyber incident involving site devices or media
trigger: A cyber incident that involves any laptop, phone, or USB drive used at the plant, or malware found on practice media by the plant
notify: Plant cyber security contact and outage coordinator by phone, confirmed in writing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - whenever a device or drive used at a plant during the last outage is involved

obligation: NRC cyber security event notification (the plant's duty)
trigger: Cyber attack affecting a licensee subject to 73.54 or 73.110
deadline: 1 hour, 4 hours, or 8 hours by event type; 24-hour recordable events
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center (by the plant)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the practice is not subject to 73.54 or 73.110 (P03 G-002). The plant decides its own reporting; the practice's 4-hour contract notice gives it the facts

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (employee records in SYS-03 or the suite, staff dose reports with Social Security numbers, client background pages). Clock starts at determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination
notify: Affected individuals (staff, former staff, and, through or with the client, client employees)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if personal information was accessed; counsel decides with the client who notifies client employees

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely: fewer than 50 staff, former staff, and client employees are in the practice's files; check the count

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
A law enforcement agency determines that notice to individuals would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay on the agency's written request for the period it specifies
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the practice (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the practice (accounting and payroll service, MSP, suite vendor) has a breach of its system
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - add to vendor contracts at renewal

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected individuals who live outside Florida (for example reactor client employees in another state named in a background page)
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law

obligation: Florida report of stolen or missing licensed material
citation: 64E-5.343, F.A.C. (as verified in this vertical's Small sample)
trigger: Licensed radioactive material found stolen, lost, or missing above the rule's quantities (for example a break-in during the incident affects the calibration room)
deadline: By telephone immediately or within 30 days depending on the quantity; written report within 30 days after the telephone report
notify: Florida Bureau of Radiation Control (by the RSO)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the calibration source or check sources are missing; not a cyber trigger by itself

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-10-05; as proposed, the practice is below the SBA size standard and meets no sector criterion. Voluntary reporting to CISA is encouraged

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI through IC3 or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Confirmed intrusion, extortion, or malware aimed at clients
deadline: As soon as practical (supports OFAC mitigation and helps clients)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - recommended, after the insurer and counsel are engaged

trigger: Suspected security incident, extortion demand, or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the breach hotline before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the practice holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
